prompt: A 400-page contract is too long to fit, so the model only sees the first part.
why: There's a maximum amount of text the model can take in at once. Going past it means some of the text is never seen.
trap: It's counted in tokens, but the clue is the maximum that fits.

prompt: In a very long chat, the bot forgot the beginning of the conversation.
tells: forgot the beginning of the conversation
why: Once the chat outgrows the window, the oldest messages are dropped to make room. That's the context window.
trap: The app does resend history, but here the history no longer fits.

prompt: The team switched to a model with a larger window so it could read the whole codebase at once.
why: A larger context window means more text fits in a single request. The choice was about the window.
trap: Model size is about capability; the window is how much text fits.

prompt: To keep long chats working, the app replaces older messages with a short summary.
tells: replaces older messages with a short summary
why: Summarizing old messages saves space so the conversation stays inside the window.
trap: History must be resent because the model is stateless, but the summary exists to fit the window.

prompt: Facts buried in the middle of a huge prompt get used less than facts at the start or end.
tells: buried in the middle of a huge prompt
why: Even inside the window, very long inputs aren't used evenly. How much you pack into the window matters.
trap: It looks like ignoring sources, but the cause is length and position in the window.

prompt: Pasting fifty documents into one request failed with an error that the input was too long.
why: The request went past the maximum the model accepts. That limit is the context window.
trap: Tokens measure it, but the error is about the limit.
